scope: Opt-in Laws-of-the-Game dead-ball rules added to the handover working model: (1) dead ball before every corroborated kickoff, (2) dead ball from the first boundary sighting back from tagged throw-ins, corners and goal kicks.

rule_details.kickoff: Formation: >=16 tracked players, each team within 1 m of its own half allowing up to two stray tracks, at least 2 s after merging gaps <=10 s; corroborated by a Smart Tagging kick-off within 5 s or an observed ball inside the centre circle near the formation break. D from formation start (or a goal-mouth entry within 150 s) to formation break. Caller-supplied period starts extend D back to a half start only within 5 min; the CLI supplies the published graded half starts, external evaluation supplies none.
rule_details.restart_anchor: For each tagged throw-in, corner or goal kick, walk back up to 60 s while the ball is unseen, beyond the line, within 1.5 m of the relevant boundary or placed in the goal area (+1 m); require a boundary sighting; D starts at the first sighting beyond the line (else first placed-ball sighting), never bridging into earlier missing-ball live play. Free kicks and untagged stoppages are not inferred.

development_history: Strict all-players formation missed both half kickoffs because of stray tracks; order statistics allow two.
Unconstrained period-start fallback created a 148 s false stoppage on external Game 1 (periods start at kickoff); now opt-in per caller.
Placed-ball goal-line extension replaced after continuing 16 s past a tagged goal kick.
Bridged restart starts added only known-live frames on Game 1; first-sighting start removed that bias.

disclosed_exception.reason_accepted: Drift guard against our own prototype, not correctness. The intended correction raises graded D 15.6% -> 21.3% toward ~38-48% known D in external provider references; all 180 external Metrica guards pass. User explicitly chose to keep.

limitations: External Metrica dead ball is encoded by a missing ball, DFL by a frozen ball; neither reproduces challenge automatic-tracking stoppage appearance.
Restart anchoring relies on automatic Smart Tagging; untagged restarts and whistle stoppages remain undetected.
One kickoff without a tag was accepted by ball corroboration only.
